Storage Proof Protocols — Statistical Detection Properties

PDP & SW — Unlimited-Challenge Schemes

Simulation: 100 blocks · one corrupted block (#74) · key size 128 bits (test mode, use ≥1024 in production for PDP) · SW sectors s=20 · L=20 blocks/challenge

1 — PDP / SW: Single-Challenge Detection Probability

When a verifier issues a challenge that samples C (PDP) or L (SW) blocks at random from a file of n blocks, and the server hides exactly one corrupted block, the probability of detection is P = C/n (or L/n). Larger files require proportionally larger challenges to maintain the same coverage. Challenges are unlimited — the verifier may run as many as needed. All three schemes (PDP, SW-Private, SW-Public) follow the same curve. Green = PDP, amber = SW-Private, purple = SW-Public; all should lie on the Theory — n=100 line.

2 — PDP / SW: Cumulative Detection Confidence (unlimited challenges)

Running k independent challenges, the probability of catching the corrupted block at least once is 1 − (1 − C/n)k. Challenges are unbounded — the verifier can keep challenging until the desired confidence is reached. Dashed lines mark 90%, 95%, and 99% confidence thresholds. Green dots: PDP at n=100, C=20. Amber dots: SW-Private at n=100, L=20. Both should follow the 20% of blocks per challenge theory line. (SW-Public uses 2 BN256 pairings per verification — too slow for 50× cumulative trials — and is omitted here; its per-challenge rate is shown in Chart 1.)

BJO-POR — Bounded-Challenge Proof of Retrievability

Simulation: 160 total blocks (data + parity, RS outer code) · V=15 blocks per challenge · Q=100 challenge budget

3 — POR: Per-Challenge Detection Probability vs V

Like PDP, POR detection per challenge follows P = V / n_total, where V is the number of blocks sampled and n_total includes both data and parity blocks. The key difference: V is fixed at protocol setup — the verifier cannot increase it dynamically. Larger parity ratios increase n_total while keeping data blocks fixed, reducing P for a given V. Theory lines shown for different (n_data, RS code) configurations. Green dots: measured rates for V ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 40} at n_total=160.

4 — POR: Cumulative Detection vs Challenge Budget (Q=100)

Each POR challenge independently has probability P = V/n_total of detecting a corrupted block. The cumulative confidence after j challenges is 1 − (1 − V/n_total)j — same formula as PDP, but capped at j = Q. Once all Q sentinels are used, no more challenges are possible. The vertical marker shows the budget limit. Green dots are measured across 10 independent key setups (each with its own KeyGen+Encode), so the PRP-deterministic block selection averages out and the empirical curve tracks the theory. Dashed lines mark 90%, 95%, 99% confidence.
